speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble with feeding and your belly looks swollen. To understand what is going on, can you tell me if your baby has been vomiting, and if so, does it ever look like green bile?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming that; since the ultrasound and images show normal results, I need to clarify the nature of the vomiting. Is the baby forceful or projectile, and does it happen after every feeding or only when lying down?

REQUEST TEST: Upper GI Series

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal ultrasound and upper GI series, have you noticed any blood or mucus mixed with the stool, or a "peanut butter" consistency? Also, has your baby passed gas normally?

REQUEST TEST: Stool_Occult_Blood
REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Stool_Study

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming those results are normal. Since we've ruled out structural blockages and bleeding, does your baby seem to have excessive gas, bloating, or a "double bubble" appearance on their belly that gets worse after feeding?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyloric Stenosis (unlikely given normal imaging) or functional obstruction; however, the specific combination of feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and the X-ray showing dilated bowel segments with no gas in the rectum strongly suggests an intestinal obstruction, possibly a meconium ileus or malrotation with volvulus that was missed on the upper GI series. Given the critical nature of an obstruction with absent rectal gas, immediate surgical consultation is warranted.
